posts.cooked:
@jffdougan: Basically I felt like the SotM demographic seemed to be guys ages 20 to 40, weighted mostly in the "25 to 35" bracket specifically. (I'm a woman in my late 30s, but I'm used to being one of the few girls in a fandom anyway.)

@ameena: High school is ages 17-18, your last section of government mandated/funded education before university. Trade/technical school is when you get trained in blue-collar jobs, usually. You get certifications rather than a degree. Everything else is gradations of university. Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, PhD.

Might as well just give your own income. Google gives pretty quick conversions, if that helps. (Type in "[number] [currency code] to USD". Like "1 EUR to USD" for example.)

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
Ameena:

I don't know what's meant by "blue collar jobs". I finished school, including Sixth Form and then did two years of Further Eduction (as opposed to Higher Education) at college but never bothered with university.Just seems like a really weird couple of questions to put on a survey about people who play a card game…

Blue-collar jobs = Stuff like factory work, construction, electricians, cosmetology, nursing, and so on. Working class, I guess would be a more universal term? In contrast to white-collar jobs like finance, office work, academia, full medical doctors.

It's pretty standard for a company to ask for stuff like income and education level; it lets them get an idea of what to develop for future products and at what price points. Having a fandom full of people who make low-to-middle incomes that mostly work with their hands is going to suggest a different culture market than, say, high-paid scientists or financiers.

I do agree that having it be heavily US-based is an issue, though. I knew that youth-level schooling differed a great deal in other countries, but I never realized that higher education did, too.
